mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 350/400 d OM656 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 inline-six diesel is a sophisticated and refined engine, but it has known weak points. Camtronic variable valve timing failure is the most significant issue, with water pump failures and CP4 fuel system sensitivity also reported. Camtronic failure can occur from 40,000-80,000 miles. Water pump failures have been reported, particularly after recalls. Bosch CP4 fuel system is sensitive to poor-quality diesel. Oil consumption and digital oil level issues are common complaints. Regular servicing with high-quality parts and fuel is essential.

mainEntity.name: What is the Camtronic problem on the Mercedes CLS 350/400 d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 engine uses Camtronic variable valve timing, which controls camshaft profiles using electromagnets. In the event of a failure, the drive electromagnets, controlled camshaft and rocker arms require replacement. Symptoms: rough running, loss of power, engine warning lights. Specialist Camtronic component replacement costs £1,000-£1,800. If ignored, valvetrain damage can occur, requiring full engine replacement. Catch it early - the repair is far cheaper than engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes CLS 350/400 d have oil consumption problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, some OM656 engines have been reported to consume oil at higher than expected rates. The digital oil level readout can also be unreliable, with levels appearing to drop suddenly. Engine oil capacity is 8.5 litres. Some owners have reported draining only 4 litres of oil. Digital oil level sensor can fail. A physical dipstick is no longer fitted - rely on the digital readout or manual checks.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLS 350/400 d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 engine has an estimated lifespan of approximately 250,000 km (155,000 miles). With proper maintenance, many units will exceed this, but Camtronic and fuel system failures can occur earlier. Estimated engine lifespan: ~250,000 km. Camtronic failure can occur from 40,000-80,000 miles. Regular oil and filter changes using Mercedes-approved 5W-30 oil are critical. Using high-quality diesel fuel prevents CP4 pump and injector issues.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes CLS 350/400 d?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a CLS 350/400 d worth £25,000-£40,000, specialist engine replacement at £5,500-£7,500 is worthwhile if the body and interior are in excellent condition. With vehicle values in this bracket, replacement is almost always justifiable. A clean, well-maintained CLS is worth saving. Rebuilt OM656 with upgraded components costs £5,500-£7,500 supply only. Compare against £7,500-£10,000 main dealer new engine quotes. If the car has other major issues, replacement may not be cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLS 350 d and CLS 400 d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both use the same OM656.929 engine family. The CLS 350 d produces 286 hp and 600 Nm, while the CLS 400 d produces 340 hp and 700 Nm. Same engine block, cylinder head and bottom end. Power difference is turbocharger specification and engine mapping. Reliability is similar between the two variants. Both are 4MATIC all-wheel drive only.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLS 350/400 d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLS 350 d and CLS 400 d arrived with the third-generation C257 CLS in 2018, powered by the OM656 3.0-litre inline-six diesel - a return to the straight-six configuration that Mercedes had not offered in a passenger car since the W124 era. The OM656 combined an aluminium block with plasma-sprayed Nanoslide cylinder coating, stepped bowl combustion, and a two-stage turbocharging system, delivering effortless torque and exceptional refinement.

milestones.description: OM656 engine introduced on the facelift S-Class (W222), then adopted across the Mercedes range
C257 CLS launched with OM656.929 diesel engine; CLS 350 d 4MATIC produces 286 hp and 600 Nm
CLS 400 d 4MATIC launched with higher-output OM656.929 producing 340 hp and 700 Nm
2023 - C257 CLS produced with OM656 engine across both diesel variants
CLS production ends; OM656 engine continues in other Mercedes models

specs.label: Configuration
specs.value: Inline-6, 24-valve, DOHC, aluminium block with Nanoslide coating

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 350/400 d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLS 350 d and CLS 400 d are powered by the OM656 3.0-litre inline-six diesel - a modern engineering masterpiece that represents Mercedes' return to the straight-six configuration. However, like any sophisticated engine, it has known weak points. The Camtronic variable valve timing system can fail, water pump issues have been reported, and the Bosch CP4 fuel system is sensitive to fuel quality. Oil consumption and digital oil level readout problems have also been reported. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Camtronic Variable Valve Timing Failure - The OM656's Defining Weakness
problems.rootCause: The Camtronic system uses electromagnets to control camshaft profiles and rocker arms. In the event of a breakdown, the drive electromagnets, controlled camshaft and rocker arms require replacement. Symptoms include rough running, loss of power, and engine warning lights.

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - A Known OM656 Weakness
problems.rootCause: Water pump failures have been reported on OM656 engines, with some occurring shortly after software recalls. Symptoms include coolant leaks, high oil temperatures (113°C on idle), and coolant temperature fluctuations. The vacuum line to the water pump can also fail, causing instability.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, coolant flush, vacuum system check

problems.recommendation: Water pump failure is a well-documented issue on the OM656. If you notice coolant loss, temperature fluctuations, or high oil temperatures, get the water pump inspected immediately. Specialist replacement at £500-£900 resolves the issue. If the vacuum system is also affected, full vacuum system repair at £800-£1,400 is required. Catch it early - overheating can cause catastrophic engine damage.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Digital Oil Level Readout Issues
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Digital Oil Level Readout Issues
problems.rootCause: The OM656 has been reported to consume oil at higher than expected rates. The digital oil level readout system can be unreliable, with the level appearing to plummet after 6,000 miles from a service. Some owners have reported draining only 4 litres of oil from an 8.5-litre capacity. The oil level sensor can also fail.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil level sensor, recalibrate system
Comprehensive oil consumption test, bore scope inspection, PCV system check
repairOptions.longevity: Required to determine root cause of oil consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 with upgraded piston rings and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil consumption is caused by worn piston rings or cylinder bore damage

problems.recommendation: The digital oil level readout on the OM656 can be unreliable. If you suspect oil consumption, have a specialist perform a manual oil check. The engine oil capacity is 8.5 litres - if you're topping up frequently, get a consumption test. A physical dipstick would be more reliable, but Mercedes has moved away from them. If oil consumption is due to worn piston rings, a rebuilt engine is the only reliable fix.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM656 oil consumption diagnosis for your Mercedes CLS 350/400 d

problems.h4: Bosch CP4 Fuel System Sensitivity - Injector and Pump Failure
problems.rootCause: The OM656 uses a Bosch CP4 high-pressure fuel pump with piezo injectors. This system is sensitive to poor-quality diesel fuel and can suffer from internal wear, leading to metal debris circulating through the fuel system. Symptoms include difficult starting, misfires, loss of power, and fuel system warning lights.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Fuel System Flush & Injector Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty injectors, flush fuel system, replace fuel filter
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; injector failure only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CP4 high-pressure pump, all injectors, fuel rail, high-pressure lines
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump debris has contaminated the entire fuel system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 with new fuel system components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if fuel system debris has caused bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: The Bosch CP4 fuel system is a known weakness across many modern diesel engines. Use high-quality diesel fuel and change the fuel filter at every service. If you experience starting issues or loss of power, get the fuel system inspected immediately. A full pump and injector replacement at £2,500-£4,000 is expensive, but it's far cheaper than a full engine replacement.
